p: An interface description is changed on IOS XE through NETCONF using openconfig-interfaces. Where does the change appear?
o: Only in a separate OpenConfig datastore that sits beside running, so show running-config doesn't include it
In the candidate datastore only, until an OpenConfig-specific commit RPC applies it
In the running configuration as native CLI, because IOS XE translates OpenConfig into its own configuration
In the running configuration, but it's lost at reload unless it's also saved through OpenConfig
e: IOS XE keeps one configuration. OpenConfig and IETF edits are mapped onto it, so they show in show running-config and are saved like any other change.

p: Match each NETCONF operation with what it does.
e: get-config reads a datastore's configuration, get adds state data, discard-changes throws away uncommitted candidate edits, and commit applies the candidate to running.
r: Copies the candidate configuration into running
Resets the candidate to match running

p: Which JSON body is valid for PUT /restconf/data/example-qos:shaper?
o: `{"example-qos:shaper": {"rate": 10000000000, "burst": 1500, "ratio": 0.75}}`
`{"example-qos:shaper": {"rate": "10000000000", "burst": 1500, "ratio": "0.75"}}`
`{"example-qos:shaper": {"rate": 10000000000, "burst": 1500, "ratio": "0.75"}}`
e: RFC 7951 encodes int64, uint64 and decimal64 as JSON strings, because many JSON parsers lose precision on large numbers. Smaller integer types, such as uint32, are JSON numbers.
c:
module: example-qos
  +--rw shaper
     +--rw rate     uint64
     +--rw burst?   uint32
     +--rw ratio?   decimal64

p: Which XML sets the interface type to the softwareLoopback identity from iana-if-type?
o: `<type xmlns:ianaift="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-interfaces">ianaift:softwareLoopback</type>`
`<type xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:iana-if-type">softwareLoopback</type>`
`<type xmlns:ianaift="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:iana-if-type">ianaift:softwareLoopback</type>`
`<type>softwareLoopback</type>`
e: In XML, an identityref value is a qualified name whose prefix must be declared in scope. Using the module name as an undeclared prefix doesn't work, and a default xmlns would move the type element itself into the wrong namespace.
c:
module: ietf-interfaces
  +--rw interfaces
     +--rw interface* [name]
        +--rw name    string
        +--rw type    identityref

iana-if-type namespace: urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:iana-if-type

p: Which RESTCONF URL reads the poe container for GigabitEthernet1/0/5?
o: `/restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F5/poe`
`/restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F5/example-poe:poe`
`/restconf/data/example-poe:poe/interface=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F5`
`/restconf/data/ietf-interfaces:interfaces/interface=GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F5/example-poe:interface/poe`
e: Augmented nodes live under the target path but belong to the augmenting module, so the path segment is module-qualified where the namespace changes. The augment doesn't create a new top-level tree.
c:
module: example-poe

  augment /if:interfaces/if:interface:
    +--rw poe
       +--rw enabled?       boolean
       +--rw max-power?     uint16
       +--ro power-drawn?   uint16

p: Which two statements about this tree are true? (Choose two.)
o: Each server must use exactly one of the two cases, because the choice has no ? marker
The URL path to udp-port includes /transport/udp/
When the tls case is used, ca-cert must be set
A server can set udp-port and tls-port at the same time
timeout must be set, because every non-key leaf is mandatory
e: A choice without ? is mandatory, and its cases exclude each other. A leaf without ? inside a case is mandatory when that case is chosen. Choice and case names never appear in paths or payloads.
c:
module: example-auth
  +--rw servers
     +--rw server* [name]
        +--rw name           string
        +--rw (transport)
        |  +--:(udp)
        |  |  +--rw udp-port?   inet:port-number
        |  +--:(tls)
        |     +--rw tls-port?   inet:port-number
        |     +--rw ca-cert     string
        +--rw timeout?       uint8

p: The image is already on the switch's flash with a matching MD5. What does file_transfer return?
o: `{'file_exists': True, 'file_transferred': True, 'file_verified': True}`
It raises an exception, because overwrite_file=False forbids an existing file
`{'file_exists': False, 'file_transferred': False, 'file_verified': False}`
`{'file_exists': True, 'file_transferred': False, 'file_verified': True}`
e: file_transfer checks for the file and its MD5 first and skips the copy when they match, reporting that nothing was transferred but the file is verified. It uses SCP, so the switch needs ip scp server enable.
c:
from netmiko import ConnectHandler, file_transfer

with ConnectHandler(**dev) as conn:
    result = file_transfer(conn,
                           source_file="cat9k_iosxe.17.12.04.SPA.bin",
                           dest_file="cat9k_iosxe.17.12.04.SPA.bin",
                           file_system="flash:", direction="put",
                           overwrite_file=False)
print(result)

p: Which send_command option returns structured data from a pyATS Genie parser, rather than from an ntc-templates template?
o: use_textfsm=True
strip_prompt=False
use_genie=True
use_ttp=True with no template
e: use_genie uses Genie's parsers when pyATS and Genie are installed, and returns the raw string if no parser matches. use_textfsm uses ntc-templates, and use_ttp needs a TTP template.

p: A team wants to inspect Cisco-IOS-XE-interfaces-oper with pyang, using the exact revision on the device. Which ncclient call retrieves it?
o: m.server_capabilities["Cisco-IOS-XE-interfaces-oper"]
m.get_schema("Cisco-IOS-XE-interfaces-oper")
m.get_config(source="running", filter=("xpath", "/interfaces-ios-xe-oper:*"))
m.get(filter=("subtree", "`<Cisco-IOS-XE-interfaces-oper/>`"))
e: get-schema, from ietf-netconf-monitoring, returns the YANG text of a module the device supports. Capabilities only list module names and revisions, and get or get-config return data, not schemas.

p: Which ncclient call saves the running configuration to startup on IOS XE?
o: m.dispatch(to_ele('`<save-config xmlns="http://cisco.com/yang/cisco-ia"/>`'))
m.copy_config(source="running", target="startup"), which IOS XE maps to write memory
m.commit()
m.edit_config(target="startup", config=running_cfg)
e: IOS XE doesn't expose a startup datastore over NETCONF, so copy-config and edit-config to startup fail. The cisco-ia save-config RPC performs the save, and commit only applies candidate to running.

p: A GET on an interface doesn't show mtu, which is still at its YANG default of 1500. Which query includes default values in the reply?
o: ?depth=unbounded
?fields=mtu
?with-defaults=report-all
?with-defaults=trim&content=all
e: Servers usually leave out leaves that hold their default. with-defaults=report-all includes them. content=all and depth=unbounded are already the defaults, and fields can't return a value the server doesn't report.

p: Which expression returns the list of GigabitEthernet entries?
o: r.json()["Cisco-IOS-XE-native:interface"]["Cisco-IOS-XE-native:GigabitEthernet"]
r.json()["Cisco-IOS-XE-native:interface"]["GigabitEthernet"]
r.json()["interface"]["GigabitEthernet"]
r.json()["Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native"]["interface"]["GigabitEthernet"]
e: The top-level member is the requested node, qualified with its module. Children in the same module aren't prefixed, and the parent native container isn't included.
c:
r = requests.get(f"{base}/data/Cisco-IOS-XE-native:native/interface",
                 auth=auth, verify="corp-ca.pem",
                 headers={"Accept": "application/yang-data+json"})
gig = ________

p: in-octets for an interface is read twice, 60 seconds apart, giving 1,000,000 and then 8,500,000. What's the average input rate?
o: 8 Mbps
125 kbps
7.5 Mbps
e: 7,500,000 octets in 60 seconds is 125,000 bytes per second, which is 1,000,000 bits per second. The * 8 converts octets to bits.
c:
a = get_counter(intf)          # 1,000,000
time.sleep(60)
b = get_counter(intf)          # 8,500,000
rate = (b - a) * 8 / 60

p: Where does this play's data end up?
o: ansible_net_interfaces, as operational data per interface
ansible_facts.interfaces, as the raw show interfaces text
A file named interfaces.json on the control node
ansible_network_resources.interfaces, as structured resource data
e: Resource facts appear under ansible_network_resources, in the same structure the resource modules accept. ansible_net_interfaces comes from the legacy interfaces gather_subset.
c:
- name: Collect interface configuration
  cisco.ios.ios_facts:
    gather_subset: min
    gather_network_resources:
      - interfaces

p: How does a team report drift between each switch's running configuration and its golden file, without changing anything?
o: Run ios_config with diff_against: intended and intended_config set to the golden file, in --check --diff mode
Run ios_config with backup: true and backup_options, then compare each backup with the golden file by hand afterwards
Run ios_command with show archive config differences, using the golden file as the argument
Run ios_config with the golden file in src and match: none, in normal mode
e: diff_against: intended compares running with intended_config and shows the result when --diff is used. With --check, nothing is pushed. match: none would push every line.

p: In an IPv6-only provisioning network, which DHCPv6 option gives a new IOS XE switch its ZTP script URL?
o: Option 43
Option 59
Option 17
Option 67
e: DHCPv6 option 59 (OPT_BOOTFILE_URL) carries the URL in IPv6, the counterpart of DHCPv4 option 67. Option 43 is the DHCPv4 vendor option, which PnP uses.

p: Which two statements about IOS XE ZTP are true? (Choose two.)
o: The Python script can run CLI commands through the cli module in Guest Shell
ZTP scripts must be written in Tcl
ZTP needs Catalyst Center to send it the Python script during onboarding
ZTP needs DHCP option 43 to find the script
ZTP only starts when the switch boots without a startup configuration
e: ZTP downloads a Python script named in option 67 (or option 59 for IPv6) and runs it in Guest Shell. Option 43 and Catalyst Center belong to PnP.

p: A RESTCONF PATCH returns this while a NETCONF script is running. What's the cause?
o: The interface already exists, so the PATCH must be sent as a POST to the parent list instead
The RESTCONF user lacks privilege 15 for writes to the running datastore
The NETCONF session holds a lock on running, so RESTCONF writes wait until it's released
The body has a key that doesn't match the URL
e: RESTCONF and NETCONF share the running datastore, so a NETCONF lock blocks RESTCONF changes, which return 409. Retry after the lock is released.

p: Match each NETCONF error-tag with its most likely cause.
e: Namespaces are case-sensitive URIs, so a typo gives unknown-namespace. create on existing data gives data-exists, a held lock gives lock-denied, and NACM refusals give access-denied.
r: Another session holds the lock on the datastore
The user isn't allowed to perform the operation
An xmlns value is misspelled, for example Cisco-IOS-XE-Native
operation="create" was used on data that's already there

p: An administrator types reload. What happens?
o: The applet and the reload run at the same time, and the message is logged
The applet logs the message, and the reload runs once the applet finishes
The reload runs first, and then the applet logs the message
The applet runs first and logs the message, and the reload isn't executed
e: With sync yes, the applet runs before the command, and _exit_status decides its fate: 0 skips the command and 1 runs it. With sync no, the command and the applet run independently.
c:
event manager applet BLOCK-RELOAD
 event cli pattern "^reload" sync yes
 action 1.0 syslog msg "reload blocked by policy"
 action 2.0 set _exit_status "0"

p: What does entry-type increment mean in this applet?
o: It fires when the CRC counter's total since the last clear reaches 100 or more
It fires when the CRC counter rises by 100 or more between polls
It fires 100 times, once for each poll after the first
It fires when the CRC counter rises by 100 or more per second
e: entry-type increment compares the change since the previous poll with entry-val, while value compares the counter itself and rate compares the change per second.
c:
event manager applet CRC-RISE
 event interface name GigabitEthernet1/0/1 parameter input_errors_crc entry-op ge entry-val 100 entry-type increment poll-interval 60
 action 1.0 syslog msg "CRC errors rising on Gi1/0/1"

p: In a Catalyst Center PnP site-claim, which part of the body supplies values for the onboarding template's variables?
o: siteId, with the variables added as query parameters
configInfo.configId, as a dict that maps each variable name to its value
imageInfo.parameters, as a list of key and value pairs
configInfo.configParameters, as a list of key and value pairs
e: configId names the template, and configParameters gives each variable as a key and value pair. imageInfo covers the image, and siteId only identifies the site.

p: What does autoBind=True do in this call?
o: It binds every network created later in the organization to this template automatically
It binds each switch in the network to the template's switch profile for its model
It re-binds the network whenever the template's configuration changes
It claims the organization's unused devices into the network as it binds
e: autoBind applies the template's switch profiles to switches of the matching model. Networks stay bound to the template without it, and binding never claims devices.
c:
dashboard.networks.bindNetwork(net_id,
                               configTemplateId=tpl_id,
                               autoBind=True)

p: Attaching a device template to a new WAN edge through SD-WAN Manager fails, reporting missing values. What's needed?
o: A reboot of the edge, so it reports those values to SD-WAN Manager
The values in the template itself, because attach requests can't carry per-device variable values
Device-specific variable values in the attach request, such as system IP, site ID and hostname
A second template containing those values, attached to the edge first
e: Templates use variables for per-device settings, and each attach must supply them, through the API body or a CSV in the GUI. The edge doesn't provide them itself.

p: What happens if no device has management IP 10.9.9.9?
o: The GET returns 404 Not Found, so r.json() raises an exception before the index
response is null, so the last line raises TypeError
dev_id is set to an empty string
The last line raises IndexError, because response is an empty list
e: A filtered list query that matches nothing still returns 200 with an empty response list, so [0] fails. Check the list's length before indexing.
c:
r = requests.get(f"{base}/dna/intent/api/v1/network-device",
                 params={"managementIpAddress": "10.9.9.9"},
                 headers={"X-Auth-Token": token}, verify="ca.pem")
dev_id = r.json()["response"][0]["id"]

p: With default settings, what does the Meraki Python SDK do when the Dashboard returns 429?
o: It retries the request straight away, in a loop, until the Dashboard accepts it
It raises APIError immediately, so the caller must retry
It waits for the time in Retry-After and retries, up to maximum_retries
It drops the request and returns None
e: wait_on_rate_limit is on by default, so the SDK sleeps for Retry-After and tries again, up to maximum_retries. After that it raises APIError.

p: Which expression gets the device list from GET /dataservice/device on SD-WAN Manager?
o: r.json()[0]
r.json()["devices"]
r.json()["response"]
r.json()["data"]
e: SD-WAN Manager replies put results in data, alongside a header with column information. response is Catalyst Center's wrapper.

p: After CSRF checking is turned on in ISE's ERS settings, every POST fails with 403, but GETs work. What must the script do?
o: Switch the body format from JSON to XML, which CSRF checking doesn't affect
Send the ERS password again in an X-CSRF-Token header on each write
Get a token from /ers/config/auth/token and send it as Authorization: Bearer on every POST, PUT and DELETE
Send a GET with X-CSRF-Token: fetch, then send the returned token in X-CSRF-Token on each write
e: With CSRF enabled, ERS issues a token in response to X-CSRF-Token: fetch, and writes must carry it. Authentication itself stays Basic.

p: What does this render?
o: Gi1/0/1 in VLAN 20, and Gi1/0/2 in VLAN 1
Gi1/0/1 in VLAN 20, and Gi1/0/2 in VLAN 20
An error, because macros need every argument
Gi1/0/1 in VLAN 20, and Gi1/0/2 with an empty VLAN
e: Macros take default values like Python functions. The second call leaves out vlan, so it gets the default of 1, and calls don't share values.

p: vlans is loaded from a CSV file, so every id is a string. What happens when this renders?
o: Rendering fails with a TypeError, because a string can't be compared with an integer
It renders every VLAN, because any non-empty string is greater than 50
It renders the VLANs whose ids sort after "50" as text, so "6" is included but "100" isn't
It renders nothing, because the comparison is always false
e: Jinja2 uses Python's comparison, and Python 3 can't order str and int. Convert first with {% if v.id | int > 50 %}.

p: port.desc is an empty string. What does this line render?
o: description, with nothing after it
description None
An error, because desc is an empty string
description UNUSED
e: default only replaces undefined values. To also replace empty strings and other false values, use default("UNUSED", true).
c: description {{ port.desc | default("UNUSED") }}

p: A uri task runs in a loop over 20 sites with register: created. Which expression lists the JSON body of each response?
o: created.json
created.results | map(attribute="content") | list
created | map(attribute="json") | list
created.results | map(attribute="json") | list
e: A looped task registers one variable whose results list holds each iteration's result. Each item has its own json key.

p: A playbook changes Meraki firewall rules, and must restore the saved rules if any task in that group fails. Which construct fits?
o: A block containing the changes, with a rescue section that restores the rules
ignore_errors: true on each task, then a final restore task
failed_when: false on each task, so the play reaches the restore task
A handler that restores the rules, notified by each change
e: rescue runs only when a task in its block fails, which suits rollback. ignore_errors and failed_when hide failures, and handlers run on changes, not on failures.

p: This task returns 415 Unsupported Media Type from Catalyst Center. What's the fix?
o: Remove to_json, so Ansible sends the dict as-is
Change method to PUT, which accepts any media type
Add return_content: true, so the response's media type matches the request's media type
Add body_format: json, so the body is sent with Content-Type: application/json
e: Without body_format, uri sends the body raw and sets no JSON content type. body_format: json serializes a dict and sets the header.
c:
- name: Create a site
  ansible.builtin.uri:
    url: "https://{{ cc_host }}/dna/intent/api/v1/site"
    method: POST
    headers:
      X-Auth-Token: "{{ token }}"
    body: "{{ site_payload | to_json }}"
    status_code: [200, 202]

p: Which body fills the blank to apply group policy 101 to a client?
o: `{"devicePolicy": "Blocked", "groupPolicyId": "101"}`
`{"devicePolicy": "Group policy", "groupPolicy": {"id": "101", "name": "Contractors"}}`
`{"devicePolicy": "Group policy", "groupPolicyId": "101"}`
`{"groupPolicy": "101"}`
e: devicePolicy chooses the policy type, and groupPolicyId names the group policy when that type is Group policy. Blocked ignores any group policy ID.
c:
PUT /networks/{networkId}/clients/{clientId}/policy
________

p: An audit must show who changed MX firewall rules in the last 24 hours. Which Dashboard API call fits?
o: `GET /networks/{networkId}/events?productType=appliance`
`GET /networks/{networkId}/appliance/firewall/l3FirewallRules?timespan=86400`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/apiRequests?timespan=86400`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/configurationChanges?timespan=86400&networkId=<id>`
e: Configuration changes record the admin, time, page and old and new values. Events cover device activity, apiRequests covers only API calls, and the rules endpoint shows only the current state.

p: A known-bad IP range must be blocked at 100 MX networks, and updated later in one place. What's the best approach?
o: Add a rule with the range to each network, and rerun a script whenever it changes
Create an organization policy object for the range, and reference it in each network's firewall rules
Bind all 100 networks to one configuration template that holds the rule, even though their other settings differ
Add the range to each network's traffic shaping rules with a low priority
e: Policy objects are defined once at the organization and referenced by firewall rules, so updating the object updates every rule that uses it. Traffic shaping limits bandwidth rather than blocking.

p: `PUT /devices/{serial}/switch/ports/GigabitEthernet1%2F0%2F12` returns 404, although the switch has 48 ports. What's wrong?
o: The slashes must not be encoded, so the portId is GigabitEthernet1/0/12
Meraki identifies switch ports by number, so the portId is 12
Port 12 must be enabled before it can be changed
Ports are changed at network level, so the serial is wrong
e: Meraki MS port IDs are the port numbers shown in the Dashboard. IOS-style interface names aren't valid IDs.

p: This Catalyst Center call returns 400 Bad Request. What's the fix?
o: Use json=payload, so the body is sent as JSON with the right header
Use files=payload, so the body is sent as multipart form data
Keep data=payload, and add Accept: application/json so Catalyst Center parses the body
Use params=payload, so the values go in the query string
e: data= with a dict sends form-encoded fields, and nested dicts are flattened. json= serializes to JSON and sets Content-Type: application/json.
c:
payload = {"type": "area",
           "site": {"area": {"name": "Auckland", "parentName": "Global/NZ"}}}
r = requests.post(f"{base}/dna/intent/api/v1/site",
                  headers={"X-Auth-Token": token}, verify="ca.pem",
                  data=payload)

p: What does dev.learn("interface") return in this test?
o: A list of dicts, one for each interface line in the output
A NETCONF reply from the interfaces-oper model
The output of show interfaces, parsed into one dict, because learn and parse are the same
A Genie Ops object, whose info dict merges several show commands into one structure
e: learn runs several commands for a feature and merges them into a device-independent structure in .info. parse handles one command at a time.
c:
intf = dev.learn("interface")
down = [n for n, d in intf.info.items()
        if d.get("enabled") and d.get("oper_status") != "up"]
assert not down, f"Interfaces down: {down}"

p: After a WAN change, a team wants to confirm, from several agents and only once, that a SaaS URL responds normally. Which approach fits?
o: Read Catalyst Center site health for the branch
Create a scheduled ThousandEyes test with a one-minute interval and leave it running
Ping the SaaS host from the edge router with Command Runner
Run a ThousandEyes instant test through the API, then read its results
e: Instant tests run once, on demand, from the chosen agents, which suits change validation. Site health and a ping don't show application-level response from the user's view.

p: Put the virl2_client calls that delete a running lab in order.
e: A lab must be stopped before its nodes can be wiped, and wiped before it can be removed.

p: Why would a team add link conditioning to a CML topology before testing an SD-WAN policy change?
o: To encrypt traffic between lab nodes the way SD-WAN tunnels do, so policies see real IPsec
To add latency, jitter and loss on links, so path-selection behavior can be tested
To raise link bandwidth above what the host's hardware can carry
To make links come up faster when the lab starts
e: Link conditioning impairs links in controlled ways, which lets policies such as application-aware routing be tested against degraded paths.

p: Which request uploads an image file from the script's host into the Catalyst Center repository?
o: `POST /dna/intent/api/v1/image/distribution` with the file in the body
`PUT /dna/intent/api/v1/image/importation` with the file base64-encoded in JSON
`POST /dna/intent/api/v1/image/importation/source/file`, as a multipart/form-data upload
`POST /dna/intent/api/v1/image/importation/source/url` with the local path
e: Local files are uploaded with source/file as a multipart upload. source/url makes Catalyst Center fetch from an HTTP or FTP server, so a local path won't work.

p: Which body tags an image as golden for access switches of one family at one site?
o: `{"imageId": "<image-id>", "siteId": "<site-id>", "deviceFamilyIdentifier": "<family-id>", "deviceRole": "ACCESS"}`
`{"imageId": "<image-id>", "deviceUuids": ["<device-id>"], "golden": true}`
`{"imageName": "cat9k_iosxe.17.12.04.SPA.bin", "site": "Global/NZ/AKL", "role": "ACCESS"}`
`{"imageId": "<image-id>", "siteId": "<site-id>", "deviceFamily": "Cisco Catalyst 9300 Switch", "role": "ACCESS", "golden": true}`
e: Golden tags apply to an image for a site, device family and device role, not to individual devices, and they use IDs rather than names.
c:
POST /dna/intent/api/v1/image/importation/golden
________

p: Which request lists the access switches with poor health in Catalyst Center?
o: `GET /dna/intent/api/v1/device-health?deviceRole=ACCESS&health=POOR`
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/site-health?deviceRole=ACCESS&health=POOR`
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/client-health?health=POOR`
`GET /dna/intent/api/v1/network-device?role=ACCESS&reachabilityStatus=Unreachable`
e: device-health filters by role, site and health category. site-health reports per site, network-device has no health score, and client-health covers clients.

p: A report needs loss and latency for every MX uplink in the organization over the last few minutes. Which call fits?
o: `GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/uplinks/addresses/byDevice`
`GET /networks/{networkId}/appliance/uplinks/usageHistory`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/uplinksLossAndLatency?timespan=300`
`GET /organizations/{organizationId}/devices/statuses`
e: uplinksLossAndLatency returns loss and latency samples per uplink and destination. statuses shows online state, and usageHistory shows traffic volume.

p: Which element turns this dynamic subscription into an on-change subscription?
o: `<yp:dampening-period>0</yp:dampening-period>`
`<yp:update-policy>on-change</yp:update-policy>`
`<yp:period>0</yp:period>`
`<yp:on-change>true</yp:on-change>`
e: yang-push uses period for periodic updates and dampening-period for on-change. A dampening period of 0 sends each change as it happens.
c:
<establish-subscription
    xmlns="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-event-notifications"
    xmlns:yp="urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-yang-push">
  <stream>yp:yang-push</stream>
  <yp:xpath-filter>/interfaces-ios-xe-oper:interfaces/interface/oper-status</yp:xpath-filter>
  ________
</establish-subscription>

p: The collector is reachable only through the switch's GigabitEthernet0/0 management port, and the receiver stays Disconnected. What's missing?
o: source-vrf Mgmt-vrf under the subscription, for the dial-out connection
source-address 10.9.0.50 in the subscription
encoding encode-xml for grpc-tcp receivers
update-policy on-change instead of periodic
e: The management port is in Mgmt-vrf, so the dial-out connection must be sourced from that VRF. source-address sets the switch's own address, not the collector's.

telemetry ietf subscription 410
 encoding encode-kvgpb

 update-policy periodic 6000

p: Before relying on a new Meraki webhook receiver, a team wants to send it a sample alert from the Dashboard API. Which calls do that?
o: `POST /networks/{networkId}/webhooks/webhookTests`, then GET the test by its ID for the result
`POST /organizations/{organizationId}/webhooks/send` with a sample payload
`GET /networks/{networkId}/webhooks/httpServers/{id}/ping`
`POST /networks/{networkId}/alerts/settings/test` with the receiver's URL and the alert type to simulate
e: webhookTests sends a sample payload to a URL, optionally with a payload template, and reports whether delivery succeeded.

p: A Catalyst Center webhook receiver requires an API key in an X-Api-Key header. Where is it configured?
o: In the event subscription's filter
In the receiver URL as a query parameter
In the headers of the REST webhook destination
In Catalyst Center's system proxy settings, which add headers to outbound requests
e: REST destinations hold custom headers, such as API keys or basic authentication, that are sent with every notification. Putting keys in URLs exposes them in logs.

p: Why are AI-driven baselines weaker at a site that came online last week?
o: Baselines are built only from configuration data, and a new site has little configuration yet
Baselines learn from history, so a new site has too little data for reliable normal ranges
New sites are excluded until their devices are upgraded
Baselines are calculated only once a year
e: Dynamic baselines model normal behavior from telemetry over time, often by hour and weekday. With little history, the ranges are wide or missing.

p: Which two limitations of AI insights in controllers should engineers keep in mind? (Choose two.)
o: Insights can't use telemetry, only the configuration stored in the controller
An insight can be wrong, so it needs checking before a change is made
Insights depend on the telemetry they receive, so missing data means missing insights
Insights only work for networks with no Cisco devices
Insights always fix the problem without approval
e: AI insights are only as good as their data, and like any model they can be wrong. Most controller AI features recommend rather than act, leaving the decision with a person.

p: An AI assistant wrote this function. Which test input exposes its bug?
o: `["down"]`
`["up", "up", "down"]`
`["down", "down"]`
e: The function returns True as soon as it finds one up, so a list with up before a down gives the wrong answer. The fix is all(s == "up" for s in states).

p: Which two are appropriate uses of an AI assistant in network automation development? (Choose two.)
o: Replacing peer review of pull requests
Explaining an unfamiliar YANG model or script before changing it
Drafting unit tests from sample device output
Keeping credentials in prompts so generated code works
Pushing generated configuration straight to production
e: Assistants help with understanding and drafting, while review, testing and change control stay with people. Credentials never belong in prompts.

p: An agent builds NETCONF payloads by inserting model output into an XML string with f-strings. What's the main risk, and the fix?
o: There's no risk, because NETCONF rejects any element it doesn't recognize
Output with extra XML can inject unintended elements; build payloads with an XML library and validate them against the YANG model
XML is slower to parse than JSON; switch to RESTCONF with JSON bodies, so injected content can't reach the device at all
The f-strings make the payload too large; compress it before sending
e: Unescaped model output can close tags and add its own elements, which may be valid YANG. Structured construction escapes values, and schema validation catches unexpected content.

p: A team wants to use a hosted LLM with device data, but policy forbids the data being kept or used for training. What addresses this?
o: Encode the data in base64 before sending it, so the provider can't read it
Use a provider agreement with zero or limited retention and no training, or a self-hosted model
Send the data only outside business hours
Use the provider's free public chat interface, which never keeps prompts or uses them for training
e: Retention and training are contractual and deployment choices. Encoding doesn't hide data, and consumer chat services often keep prompts.

p: Which MCP request does a client send to fetch the content of this?
o: resources/list, which returns each resource's content
tools/call, with name sites
resources/read, with uri config://sites
prompts/get, with name sites
e: resources/list returns resource names and URIs, and resources/read returns a resource's content. tools/call and prompts/get are for tools and prompts.

p: A FastMCP tool backs up 200 devices and takes several minutes. How can it show the client how far it's got?
o: Call print() after each device, because the client reads the server's stdout as progress updates
Raise a ToolError every 10 devices with the count so far
Call await ctx.report_progress(progress=done, total=200) as each device finishes
Return partial results every few devices, and keep the tool running
e: Context.report_progress sends progress notifications that clients can display. A tool returns once, print corrupts stdio, and ToolError ends the call.

p: A FastMCP server with tools that change Meraki settings will be exposed over HTTP to agents on other hosts. Which two should be in place? (Choose two.)
o: A non-standard port, which keeps unauthorized clients out
Authentication, such as bearer tokens the server verifies
The server running as root, so tools never fail on permissions
TLS, directly or through a reverse proxy
Logging turned off, so tool arguments aren't recorded
e: Remote MCP servers are APIs and need authentication and encryption. An unusual port isn't access control, and audit logs and least privilege should stay.
